description: S4 cluster: membership, quorum, peers, hinted handoff, repair and nodes, from the metrics every cluster node exports at /metrics. Every metric exists from the node's start at zero, so an empty graph means nothing happened.

panels.title: Members not alive
panels.description: The most members of the pool any one node holds not alive. 0 is a healthy pool. A configured member a node has not heard from since it started counts as dead on that node.

panels.title: Members by status, as each node sees them
panels.description: s4_cluster_nodes: the members of S4_POOL_NODES by status as each node sees them, itself included. On every node the statuses add up to the pool size. suspect and left stay at 0: a suspected member is reported straight as dead, and a stopping node does not announce that it leaves.

panels.title: Peer up, as each node sees it
panels.description: s4_cluster_peer_up: 1 while the node holds the peer alive. A peer down on every node is down; a peer down on one node only is a network problem between the two.

panels.title: Quorum operations
panels.description: s4_quorum_operations_total: quorum operations each node coordinated, per second, by whom they served (client: requests; system: the node's own work), operation and outcome.

panels.title: Quorum failures
panels.description: Quorum operations that failed, per second. quorum_not_met is the one to alert on: fewer replicas answered than the operation needs.

panels.title: Quorum latency p50 / p99
panels.description: s4_quorum_duration_seconds of the operations that served requests (origin client) over every selected node. The buckets of all nodes add up, so this is the percentile of the cluster as clients see it.

panels.title: Calls to peers
panels.description: s4_peer_requests_total: calls each node made to each peer, per second, by outcome. cancelled is a call the caller stopped waiting for, usually because the quorum was already reached.

panels.title: Failed calls by peer
panels.description: Calls to a peer that failed, per second. skipped means gossip holds the peer dead and no call was made. Failures that pile up on one peer point at the node that holds the cluster back.

panels.title: Peer latency p50 / p99
panels.description: s4_peer_request_duration_seconds: how long each peer took to answer, over every selected node.

panels.title: Hints pending by target
panels.description: s4_hints_pending: hints the selected nodes hold on disk for each peer. They are delivered once the peer is back; a count that stays up while the peer is alive is not being delivered.

panels.title: Hints stored, delivered, dropped
panels.description: Hints per second. A dropped hint (full, expired, rejected, superseded, ambiguous) is a write the replica does not get from hinted handoff.

panels.title: Read repairs
panels.description: s4_read_repairs_total: writes to stale replicas found by a quorum read, per second.

panels.title: Anti-entropy
panels.description: Rounds by how they ended, keys found in different versions on the node and its peer, and what settling them came to, per second.

panels.title: Anti-entropy round duration p50 / p99
panels.description: s4_anti_entropy_round_duration_seconds: how long the anti-entropy rounds that ran took, skipped rounds aside.

panels.title: Repair frontier lag
panels.description: s4_repair_frontier_lag_seconds: age of the oldest repair frontier boundary over the peers of the pool, as of the node's last anti-entropy round.

panels.title: Tombstones active
panels.description: s4_tombstones_active: tombstones left on each node after its last GC pass.

panels.title: Tombstones purged
panels.description: s4_tombstones_purged_total: tombstones removed by GC, per second.

panels.title: Disk used
panels.description: The filesystem under each node's data directory, as the node measures it for its peers every 30 seconds. A node that cannot measure it reports a total of 0 and is left out.

panels.title: Scrubber: blobs verified
panels.description: s4_scrubber_blobs_scanned_total: blobs each node checked against their CRC32, per second. A rate that never rises means the scrubber finds no volumes to walk.

panels.title: Bit rot found and healed
panels.description: Damaged blobs each node found, and repaired from a replica, in each interval of the graph. Found minus healed is damage the node still carries.

panels.title: Scrubber scan progress
panels.description: s4_scrubber_scan_progress: how far each node's current full scan has got.

panels.title: Version and edition
panels.description: s4_build_info: the version of each node and the edition it runs as. An Enterprise build without a licence runs, and reports, as ce.

panels.title: Licence days left
panels.description: s4_license_expiry_timestamp_seconds, only on nodes running under an Enterprise licence. Empty on Community Edition.

panels.title: Topology epoch
panels.description: s4_cluster_epoch: the topology epoch of each node. The nodes of a pool agree on it.

panels.title: Unenforced versioning and Object Lock
panels.description: s4_bucket_unenforced_configs: buckets whose versioning or Object Lock a node stores from an earlier release, which accepted them in cluster mode. Cluster mode enforces neither: objects in those buckets keep no versions and can be deleted under retention. 0 is expected; the buckets are listed in /api/admin/cluster/health of each node.

panels.title: Configurations read through the quorums
panels.description: s4_bucket_config_quorum_reads: 1 once every node of the pool adopted the bucket configurations an earlier release kept on single nodes and this node reads them through the quorums; 0 while it answers from its own copy first. Every node at 1 is expected; a node at 0 for long waits for a node of its pool that is down or runs an earlier release.

panels.title: Configuration adoption
panels.description: s4_bucket_config_adoption_keys_total: bucket configurations an earlier release kept on a single node, by what adopting them came to, per second. adopted: copied to the replicas of their key; superseded: a replica held a newer version; orphaned: the bucket was deleted since; deferred: left for the next pass, every 30 s, usually while a replica is down. Moves only after an upgrade from such a release.

panels.title: Bucket records stage
panels.description: s4_bucket_metadata_stage: where the node is in the move of the pool's bucket records and settings to as many replicas as the pool survives failures for. 0 legacy (three replicas), 1 dual write (writes go to both layouts while each node brings the older records over), 2 read new, 3 settled. Every node at 3 is expected; a node below 3 for more than a few minutes waits for a node of its pool that is down or runs an earlier release, which /api/admin/cluster/health names.

panels.title: Bucket records replicas
panels.description: s4_bucket_metadata_replication_factor: the replicas the pool keeps each bucket's records and settings on once the move settled: the data's in a replicated pool, 5 for RS 4+2 on six nodes, or S4_BUCKET_METADATA_REPLICATION_FACTOR. Every node of a pool must show the same number.

panels.title: Bucket records backfill
panels.description: s4_bucket_metadata_backfill_keys_total: bucket records and settings the backfill brought to the new replicas during the move, by outcome, per second. copied: a new replica got them; already: every replica held them; unconfirmed: a refused write left them on too few nodes, and they stay as they were; failed: a replica did not answer, and the next pass, 10 s later, counts them again; dropped: a record an earlier release made up on a node that did not keep it, removed. Moves only during a move.

panels.title: Bucket records backfill passes
panels.description: s4_bucket_metadata_backfill_passes_total: backfill passes, per second, by whether every key settled. The move goes on once a pass is complete on every node; incomplete passes repeat every 10 s while a node of the pool does not answer.

panels.title: Fenced bucket record writes
panels.description: s4_bucket_metadata_fenced_writes_total: writes of bucket records and settings this node refused, per second, because they came from a node of an earlier release, or one behind the pool, after the move began. Anything above zero means such a node is in the pool: it cannot create or delete buckets until it runs this release.

panels.title: Fenced IAM writes
panels.description: s4_iam_fenced_writes_total: writes of users and root's state this node refused, per second, because they were made outside the current lease of IAM changes: by a node whose lease ran out or was taken over by a later one. A short burst after a node stalled or was cut off is fencing at work; a steady rate means a node keeps writing with a lease it no longer holds.

panels.title: IAM copy lag
panels.description: s4_iam_replica_lag_seconds: how long ago a majority of the pool last agreed with each node's copy of users and keys. Below a second in a healthy pool; past S4_IAM_MAX_STALENESS_SECS the node answers 503 to IAM credentials.

panels.title: IAM credentials refused
panels.description: s4_iam_auth_refused_total: requests with IAM credentials a node answered 503 per second, by reason: starting (catching up after a start) or stale (cut off from most of the pool). Root and the credentials of the environment are never refused this way.

panels.title: IAM epoch
panels.description: s4_iam_epoch_applied: wall time of the newest change of users or root's state each node holds, deletes included. The nodes of a pool meet on one value a moment after a change; one that stays behind missed changes.

panels.title: IAM adoption pending
panels.description: s4_iam_adoption_pending: 1 while some node of the pool keeps IAM users of its own that the pool has not taken over — an earlier release, or the node as a single node, stored them on it alone — and IAM changes are refused (409 IamAdoptionPending). A fresh pool shows 1 for a moment after it starts, until every node announced it keeps none; after an upgrade it stays 1 until the operator decides through /api/admin/iam/adoption.

panels.title: IAM configuration mismatch
panels.description: s4_iam_config_mismatch: 1 while the live nodes of the pool are configured differently for IAM, by setting: root (root's name or password), jwt_secret (S4_JWT_SECRET) or encryption_key (the key the secrets of S3 credentials are encrypted with). The cluster health is critical meanwhile and names the node that differs.

panels.title: IAM secrets by encryption key
panels.description: s4_iam_records_by_key_id: IAM users whose S3 secret each node holds encrypted with each key, by key id; key_id="clear" counts secrets still in clear text. After a new S4_IAM_ENCRYPTION_KEY the old key's series falls to 0 once every secret is encrypted again; then the old key can be removed.

panels.title: Pool generation
panels.description: s4_pool_generation: epoch of the pool generation each node places keys by. While the pool grows it is the one the keys move from; when the growth settles every node shows the grown epoch. Nodes that disagree for longer than a growth takes point at a node that has not settled, which GET /api/admin/cluster/rebalance on it explains.

panels.title: Ranges of a growing pool
panels.description: s4_rebalance_ranges: ranges of the ring by state, as each node applies them. pending: not begun; streaming: being moved; verified: compared; cut_over: read through the grown generation. All 0 while the pool does not grow; during a growth cut_over climbs to the total, then the pool settles and every state drops back to 0.

panels.title: Left to hand over
panels.description: s4_rebalance_remaining_bytes: estimate of what each old node still has to go through before it handed its keys to the new owners — its stored bytes in the share of its ranges not handed over. It counts erasure-coded shards too, which do not move, so on such a pool it is an upper bound. 0 once a node handed over everything.

panels.title: Keys and bytes moved
panels.description: s4_rebalance_keys_total and s4_rebalance_bytes_total: keys each node brought to the new owners of a growing pool, and the bytes of the copies it sent, per second. The pace is capped by S4_REBALANCE_MAX_KEYS_PER_SEC and S4_REBALANCE_MAX_BYTES_PER_SEC, and gives way while clients keep the node busy.

panels.title: Move paused
panels.description: s4_rebalance_paused: 1 while a node's move is paused. operator: paused through POST /api/admin/cluster/rebalance/pause, until it is resumed; no_room: a new owner has less free space than S4_REBALANCE_MIN_FREE_RATIO, and the keys meant for it wait until space is freed.

panels.title: Move errors
panels.description: s4_rebalance_errors_total: keys that failed a try to reach their new owners, by reason, per second. checksum: a copy failed its CRC32 or SHA-256 and was taken from another replica; unavailable: a replica did not answer; ambiguous: no quorum confirmed the newest version; storage and placement: this node's own. Each key is tried again; a steady stream from one node names a replica that holds the move back.

panels.title: Fenced pool generation writes
panels.description: s4_pool_generation_fenced_writes_total: writes a node refused because their coordinator placed them by an earlier pool generation than the one the pool moves to. A node of an earlier release, or one restarted with the pool's earlier S4_POOL_NODES, writes so; restart it with the current release and configuration.

panels.title: Records pending migration
panels.description: Single-mode records this node still needs to bring to every cluster owner. Wait for zero before switching clients.

panels.title: Records migrated or superseded
panels.description: Single-mode records finished in this process, by outcome. A restart resets the counters and completed records are not counted again.

panels.title: HTTP requests by status
panels.description: http_requests_total: requests the selected nodes answered, per second, by status code.

panels.title: HTTP latency p50 / p99
panels.description: http_request_duration_seconds over every selected node.

title: S4 Cluster
